title: Britain's 1951 zebra stripes were painted onto existing stud-marked crossings; crossings can have both studs and stripes

sources.publisher: Learning on Screen (News on Screen archive)
sources.title: News on Screen document NoS_104397 (1951 notice on pedestrian crossings, linked to a British Pathé story)
sources.license: Learning on Screen website terms (facts only)
sources.note: PDF 下載時回應 503／連線被重設，事實取自 2026-10-09 搜尋結果中該文件的內容摘錄：白色條紋剛漆在選定的既有穿越道上，配合 1951 年 10 月 31 日生效的穿越道新規定

sources.title: The Highway Code: Rules for pedestrians (1 to 35)
The Zebra, Pelican and Puffin Pedestrian Crossings Regulations and General Directions 1997, Schedule 1

facts.text: In 1951, white stripes were painted onto chosen crossings that were already in use, ahead of new crossing rules that began on 31 October 1951.
Britain's Highway Code tells people on foot to cross between the studs or over the zebra markings, so one crossing can have both studs and stripes.
Britain's 1997 crossing rules put the black-and-white stripes inside the limits of a zebra crossing and describe two lines of studs, which may also be left out.

notes: 補 pedestrian-crossing-mxb04 的不足（ai.mx.c3c7df 的 fact_check）：1951 年是在原本用兩排圓釘標示的穿越道上加漆條紋，圓釘沒有拆除。2026-10-09 的 fact_check 另查到 Commercial Motor 1951-07-13 報導新規定保留圓釘（archive.commercialmotor.com，不在白名單，只作查核參考，不列為來源）。現行 1997 年規章允許省略圓釘，所以題組不寫「現在每條斑馬線都有圓釘」。
